chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the discipline of the child and the slave, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Five, or six, and be kind.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic approach to disciplining children and slaves according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*’s chapter on miscellaneous rulings, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the pedagogical principle of *urfuq* (gentleness) as the cornerstone of raising children and slaves. It reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing authority with compassion, suggesting that discipline should be rooted in affection rather than harshness to foster moral development.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,
‘I spoke to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding disiplining of the child and the owned (slave), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Five, or six, and be kind’.
